full_before_question.:question/worked-solution:
Remember that the scalar triple product $a\cdot (b\times c)$ is just the determinant of the matrix whose rows are given by $a,$ $b,$ and $c.$

So, we have

$$
\begin{aligned}a\cdot (b\times c) & =\begin{vmatrix}-1 & 2 & 4 \\ 0 & 3 & 1 \\ 2 & 5 & 0\end{vmatrix} \\  & =(-1)\cdot \begin{vmatrix}3 & 1 \\ 5 & 0\end{vmatrix}\,-\,2\cdot \begin{vmatrix}0 & 1 \\ 2 & 0\end{vmatrix}\,+\,4\cdot \begin{vmatrix}0 & 3 \\ 2 & 5\end{vmatrix} \\  & =(-1)\,(3\cdot 0-1\cdot 5)\,-\,2\,(0\cdot 0-1\cdot 2)\,+\,4\,(0\cdot 5-3\cdot 2) \\  & =(-1)\,(-5)\,-\,2\,(-2)\,+\,4\,(-6) \\  & =5+4-24 \\  & =-15.\end{aligned}
$$

evidence.independent_math: (-1,2,4) dot ((0,3,1) cross (2,5,0)) = 5+4−24 = −15. Existing canonical value and full determinant solution agree.
